lobbying_activities.description: - Fighting Trade Cheats Act of 2025 (H.R. 1284/S.2808) - Support bill which aims to strengthen enforcement of U.S. customs laws and deter trade fraud, particularly concerning customs violations and unfair trade practices. - Leveling the Playing Field Act 2.0 (H.R.1548/S.691/) - Support bill that updates U.S. trade remedy law to combat Chinas anti-free market trade practices. - Protecting American Industry & Labor from International Trade Crimes Act (H.R. 1869) - Support bill which sets up a structure to criminally prosecute serious trade crimes. - Tariffs and Section 232 - highlighted ongoing concerns with dumping and transshipment issues related to iron castings. - Brazilian pig iron - opposition to proposed tariffs on Brazil related to pig iron which is essential for domestic iron foundries. - USMCA - Urge stronger provisions in USMCA to combat transshipments of metal castings through Mexico.

GRID Power Act - (H.R. 1047/S.465) - The bill would enable grid operators to expedite consideration of power generation projects that improve the reliability of the electric grid. Need for Permitting Reform
OSHA's Proposed Rule on Heat Injury and Illness Prevention in Outdoor and Indoor Work Settings - discussed impact of proposed rule on metalcasters.

-Standardizing Permitting and Expediting Economic Development (SPEED) Act (HR 4746) - Support bill would limit the scope of permitting reviews and restrain legal challenges for projects under the National Environmental Policy Act - eliminates costly delays that plague the current permitting process. - H.R. 6398, the Reducing and Eliminating Duplicative Environmental Regulations Act - Support The RED Tape Act would eliminate the mandate that the Environmental Protection Agency review a project already subject to environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act. -H.R. 6409, the Foreign Emissions and Nonattainment Clarification for Economic Stability Act - Support The FENCES Act would protect manufacturing investment here in the United States by preventing emissions from outside the US from being used in calculations that determine the issuance of a permit. Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (WRDA 2026) - H.R. 9497/S.4949 - WRDA advances key interests related to ports, inland waterways, levees, dams, wetlands, watersheds and coastal restoration.Support Senate provisons related reauthorization of the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (DWSRF), Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF), and Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA) programs at the authorization levels. Prove It Act of 2025 - H.R.1163/ S. 495 - Support bill to ease regulatory burden on small manufacturers by requiring agencies to evaluate impact on and consider input from small businesses throughout the regulation process. Promoting Efficient Review for Modern Infrastructure Today (PERMIT) Act, H.R.3898 - Support modernization of regulatory authorities under the Clean Water Act-reforms that are critical to metalcasters ability to build and expand. -Support Senate introduction of permitting reform legislation.

- Support Developing Overseas Mineral Investments and New Allied Networks for Critical Energies Act, or DOMINANCE Act, H.R.7037, which would create new offices and high-level positions to boost mineral diplomacy and counter Chinas supply chain dominance. Directs U.S. to work with allies and partners to fortify supply chains and boost domestic production of critical minerals. - Prove It Act of 2025 (H.R. 1163/ S. 495) - Support bill that strengthens the Regulatory Flexibility Act by improving transparency in regulatory process by requiring agencies to fully disclose and justify their analyses of small business impacts.

- BUILD America 250 Act - H.R. 8870- Support reauthorization of the Surface Transportation Bill and robust investment levels for federal infrastructure, allocates significant backing to bridge repair and replacement programs, and funding for public transit and for passenger rail. - Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (H.R.8730/ S. 4429) - Support bill that prohibits the import, manufacture, and sale of connected vehicles, software, and critical hardware linked to foreign adversaries like China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran to safeguard U.S. national security and domestic manufacturing.

21st Century ROAD to Housing Act - Support bill that includes dozens of provisions aimed at increasing housing supply and bringing down costs. Support ROAD to Housing Act of 2025 (S.2621) - Support package aimed at increasing housing supply and improving affordability and access to housing.

- FY27 Defense Appropriations - Support vital research for the Aluminum Castings Performance Initiative (ACPI) at $10 million, as aluminum castings are foundational to our national defense and utilized in aircraft, landing gear, naval propulsion systems, armored vehicle structures, and much more.

COPPER Act - H.R. 8277 - Urged support for bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code to designate copper as a critical mineral and includes ore extraction costs in the Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit (45X).

FY27 Interior-EPA Appropriations - Ensure Robust Funding for Critical Water Infrastructure Programs - Reauthorize and maintain at or above current funding levels through FY2031 for: - Clean Water and Drinking Water State Revolving Funds (SRFs); Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA); Grant programs that support small and disadvantaged communities;Lead service line replacements; Reduction of lead in drinking water and the removal of emerging contaminants programs; and Maintain Buy America preferences for iron, steel, and manufactured products, as well as improving and tightening waiver processes.

We will be closely following actions of the House and the Senate as they work to add Congressional legislation to supplement the local and state efforts. Worked in reference to the FY27 Energy and Water Appropriations bill to include funding for Federal efforts to address the aftermath of the Eaton Canyon fire and how some of these funds could be sent to cities in the San Gabriel Valley. The funding would be for protection of the local aquifers from post-fire damage. The bill numbers for funding for this request is located in the Interior and Environment Apprropriations bill of HR 9171, H. Report-119-687, page 245, Representative Cisneros. As of this date, the Energy and Water Appropriations FY26 Appropriations has not been passed by either House of Congress. Our client will continue to work in terms of supporting Congressional Priorty funding in the Energy and Water Appropriations ill when it hopefully taken up by the Congress.

H.R.7567- Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 (House Farm Bill) engage in efforts related to conservation and forestry contained in the legislation.

S.5368 Water Cyber Shield Act. Support and engage on issues related to robust statutory cybersecurity requirements for the water sector to increase resilience and sustainability. H.R.7129 Water Power Research and Development Reauthorization Act. Support and engage on issues related to water power research, development, demonstration, and commercial application activities, including desalination. H.R.10083 Water Technology Resilience and Reauthorization Act. Support and engage on issues related to the reauthorization of the Advanced Drinking Water Technology Grant Program under the Safe Drinking Water Act.

Review and engage on issues associated with the implementation of the 2024 Water Resources Development Act - P.L.118-272. Engage on water infrastructure issues relating to the development of the 2026 Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) including H.R. 9497 (House WRDA bill) and S.4949 (Senate WRDA bill).

H.R. 4509 - NOPAIN for Veterans Act Advocated for legislation ensuring VA providers can access a full range of individualized, evidence-based post-surgical pain management options, including non-opioid therapies, without overly restrictive one-size-fits-all barriers. Argued that clinical judgment must guide acute pain care for veterans recovering from surgery or serious procedures. Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102 / S. 1032) - Concurrent Receipt for Combat-Injured Retirees Advocated for elimination of the dollar-for-dollar offset that reduces retirement pay for approximately 52,000 combat-injured veterans medically retired before completing 20 years of service. Supported the House discharge petition to bring H.R. 2102 to a floor vote, which reached 218 signatures on September 15, 2026, and urged inclusion of the Star Act in the FY27 NDAA conference agreement. Communicated that this 'wounded veteran tax' breaks faith with those who sacrificed most and that concurrent receipt of earned retirement pay and VA disability compensation should be permitted. Veterans Mental Health & Suicide Prevention - VA Staffing, Telehealth, In-Person Care Advocated for a comprehensive strategy to address veteran suicide (averaging 17.6 deaths per day). Communicated support for increased VA mental health staffing, expanded telehealth services to reach rural and underserved veterans, and preservation of in-person mental health care. Emphasized that telehealth must complement, not replace, VA mental health professionals. Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy (HBOT) - VA Pilot Program for PTSD/TBI Advocated for VA implementation of pilot programs to evaluate Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy as a covered treatment for veterans with PTSD and Traumatic Brain Injuries, citing studies indicating HBOT can significantly reduce PTSD symptoms and improve cognitive function. Urged Congress to direct the VA to expand access to evidence-based alternative treatments, and supported the TCAVA provision (Sec. 307) requiring GAO to update its report on HBOT as a treatment for TBI and PTSD. Guard and Reserve GI Bill Parity Act Advocated for legislation ensuring all service days count toward Post-9/11 GI Bill eligibility for National Guard and Reserve members who serve alongside active-duty counterparts. Communicated that existing education benefit disparities are inequitable given equivalent operational contributions. Student Veteran Benefit Restoration Act Advocated for legislation ensuring veterans who lose education benefits due to school closures or fraud have those benefits restored. Communicated that veterans should not suffer financial losses due to circumstances beyond their control. Veteran Caregiver Reeducation, Reemployment, and Retirement Act Advocated for comprehensive reforms to support family caregivers of veterans, including provisions addressing financial security, career reemployment, and retirement benefits for individuals who sacrifice their own professional advancement to provide uncompensated daily care. Communicated that caregivers are the backbone of the veterans' care system and must not be left behind when caregiving roles end. Survivor Benefits - DIC Modernization (Love Lives On Act / Remarriage Restriction Repeal / Rate Modernization) Advocated for elimination of the DIC remarriage age restriction and modernization of DIC rates to reflect the true cost of sacrifice. Supported the Love Lives On Act, which removes the DIC remarriage bar and restores Survivor Benefit Plan annuities for surviving spouses who remarried before age 55, and extension of increased DIC to survivors of veterans who died from ALS. Communicated that surviving spouses should not be forced to choose between financial security and honoring their loved one's wishes, and that current restrictions impose unnecessary financial penalties on Gold Star families. Protecting Veterans' Disability and Retirement Pay from Budget Reductions Advocated against any legislative or executive action to reduce veterans' disability compensation or retirement pay to balance the federal budget. Communicated alignment with VA Secretary Doug Collins's stated opposition to cutting earned veterans' benefits, and emphasized that reducing these benefits undermines national trust and deters future enlistment. Written Informed Consent for Black Box Medications (VA Policy / Written Informed Consent Act) Advocated for VA policy and legislation requiring written informed consent before prescribing psychiatric medications with black box warnings. Communicated that veterans deserve transparency, patient autonomy, and the ability to make fully informed decisions regarding high-risk medications. Protecting the VA as an Institution - Structural and Operational Integrity Advocated for preservation of VA capacity, organizational structure, and services for enrolled veterans. Communicated concerns about any restructuring or resource reductions that would diminish the VA's ability to deliver timely, high-quality care and benefits to the veteran community. H.R. 9237 / S. 4744 - Take Care of America's Veterans Act (TCAVA) Communicated AFSA's conditional support for the package, which includes the Major Richard Star Act, the Love Lives On Act, the Vets Opportunity Act, the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act, reauthorization of the SSgt Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program, an updated GAO review of hyperbaric oxygen therapy, and Transition Assistance Program and SkillBridge improvements. Expressed concern with legislating changes to the VA Schedule for Rating Disabilities for tinnitus and sleep apnea as a cost offset (Sec. 108), and insisted that any changes protect existing ratings and apply only to future claims. H.R. 5339 - Susan E. Lukas 9/11 Servicemember Fairness Act Advocated for legislation establishing a presumption of service connection for certain diseases in veterans who served on active duty at the Pentagon Reservation between September 11 and November 19, 2001. Joined the bill's sponsor and the Reserve Organization of America at a September 10, 2026 press conference urging Congress to pass the bill.

S. 4784 / H.R. 8800 - FY27 NDAA, Sec. 765 (Study on Military Health System) Met with Senate Armed Services Committee staff alongside The Military Coalition to support the Section 765 independent study of the Military Health System. Urged that military and veterans service organizations be engaged as the study is designed and carried out, citing the Military Compensation and Retirement Modernization Commission as an example of the value of that engagement. S. 4784 / H.R. 8800 - FY27 NDAA Conference, Quality of Life Provisions Urged conferees to retain or reconcile House and Senate quality of life provisions, including: House Sec. 735 (pregnancy as a qualifying event for TRICARE Select, pilot); House Sec. 631 and Senate Sec. 633 (food, child care, and housing information at PCS); Sec. 621 (commissary and exchange patron expansion and the House bag-fee prohibition); Sec. 702 (expanded dental access for dependents at military treatment facilities); House Sec. 745 / Senate Sec. 711 (wellness checks for injured or sick members); Sec. 611 (extension of bonus and special pay authorities and the Basic Needs Allowance housing allowance exclusion); House Sec. 557 / Senate Sec. 531 (UCMJ coverage of AI-generated intimate images); and House Sec. 747 / Senate Sec. 549A (transition of military medics to civilian health careers). S. 4784 / H.R. 8800 - FY27 NDAA, Pay, Housing, Family, and TRICARE Provisions Advocated for the Senate 3.6 percent basic pay raise (Sec. 602); housing allowance improvements, including the House Basic Needs Allowance housing allowance exclusion, lower trigger for temporary BAH increases, and mandatory CONUS COLA (House Secs. 611-614; Senate Sec. 603); military spouse employment provisions (Senate Secs. 561-562; House Sec. 577); TRICARE T-5 transition protections and oversight (House Secs. 734, 742; Senate Secs. 701, 705, 706); the Exceptional Family Member Program review (Senate Sec. 563); blast overpressure protections (House Secs. 233, 1709); and a GAO study of SkillBridge (House Sec. 1723). FY27 NDAA Conference - The Military Coalition Letter to Conferees (Retired Affairs Committee) Co-led a coalition letter to FY27 NDAA conferees urging inclusion of the Major Richard Star Act and repeal of the 180-day waiting period for appointing retired members to Department of War civilian positions (Retain Skilled Veterans Act), and recommending deletion of the Expanding America's National Cemetery Act provision. TRICARE T-5 Managed Care Support Contract Transition - Beneficiary Access Communicated to Defense Health Agency officials the access problems members reported after the T-5 contractor transition (TriWest and Humana), and urged accountability for network adequacy, provider directory accuracy, and advance beneficiary notification of contract transitions. Military Family GI Bill Promise Act (H.R. 4540) / Post-9/11 GI Bill Transferability Entitlement Act (S. 4237) Advocated for legislation ensuring transferable Post-9/11 GI Bill education benefits can be passed to dependents by servicemembers who separate or have children later in life or after separation, including S. 4237, which would allow any member who has completed ten years of service to transfer benefits to dependents at any time, on active duty or as a veteran. Emphasized that no servicemember should lose benefits they rightfully earned and that transferability is a powerful family-focused recruiting and retention tool. Pay Our Troops Act (S. 3002 / H.R. 5401) Advocated for passage of legislation guaranteeing uninterrupted military pay during government shutdowns or continuing resolution periods. Communicated to committee staff and bill sponsors that pay disruptions harm retention, readiness, and financial stability of enlisted Airmen and Guardians and their families. AFSA's primary priority is full-year defense appropriations on time; this bill serves as a critical backstop. IVF for Military Families Act (H.R. 2557 / S. 1231) Advocated for TRICARE coverage of in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatments for servicemembers whose ability to start families has been impaired by service-connected injuries or deployments. Emphasized closing the gap between military and federal civilian workforce healthcare access and the importance of family planning support to retention and holistic readiness. H.R. 6976 - Codify Duty Status Reform Advocated for legislation codifying duty status reforms for National Guard and Reserve members to ensure appropriate benefits and protections apply during all periods of service, including those not covered under traditional active duty orders. H.R. 6796 - Military CARE Act Advocated for provisions supporting military caregiver support programs and expanding resources available to servicemembers and their families during and after service. S. 2448 / H.R. 4768 - Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act Advocated for parity in healthcare access, affordability, and quality between military families and the federal civilian workforce, reducing out-of-pocket costs and improving the overall TRICARE benefit. H.R. 4381 / S. 2239 - Improving Access to Prenatal Care for Military Families Act Advocated for legislation improving access to prenatal care for military families, addressing gaps in TRICARE coverage and geographic access to maternity services for servicemembers stationed at remote or OCONUS installations.

R. 9373/S. 4829, the Air Carrier Access Amendment Act (ACAAA) of 2026. United Spinal, along with other disability organizations, submitted comments in response to the Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a New Approval of Information Collection: Passenger Evacuation Experience Survey published on July 15, 2026. The comments read in part, The request for comments addresses approval for a new survey to gather information on passengers' experiences during an emergency evacuation or rapid deplanement of a passenger transport category aircraft. Surveys can be one of the best methods to understand areas for improving guidance. Data is necessary to evaluate passenger behavior, passenger flow, passenger experiences - including for passengers with disabilities - and to evaluate passenger decision-making. We recommend the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proceed with the passenger survey to ensure that all passengers can relay their experience and FAA can work to improve evacuation and rapid deplanement procedures, including for passengers with disabilities. https://downloads.regulations.gov/FAA-2026-7671-0002/attachment_1.pdf

lobbying_activities.description: United Spinal advocates for H.Res. 1586: Introduced by Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI) and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) on September 28, 2026, this bipartisan resolution recognizes and honors the 27th anniversary of Olmstead v. L.C. and affirms that the decision reflects congressional intent under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) for individuals with disabilities to live and receive services in integrated community settings. https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-resolution/1586 United Spinal advocated against a June 18, 2026 DOJ Office of Legal Counsel memo saying that federal disability rights laws do not provide that people with disabilities be served in their own homes and communities. The memo says that neither Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) nor Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act says that people with disabilities should be served in the most integrated setting appropriate. This memo is inconsistent with decades of well-established law and the U.S. Supreme Courts decision in Olmstead v. L.C. The DOJs new position is a complete reversal of the positions it has taken over the 27 years since the Olmstead decision.

lobbying_activities.description: United Spinal continues to advocate for H.R. 4206, the CONNECT for Health Act. United Spinal continues to advocate with members of Congress for increased federal funding for the Spinal Cord Injury Model Systems as well as the Burn Model Systems and the Traumatic Brain Injury Model Systems. Increased funding at all three Model Systems, including the Model Systems Knowledge Translation Center is needed to translate data, research, and clinical knowledge into resources to benefit the SCI, TBI and burn injury communities. This includes inserting language into the FY27 Labor-HHS-Education appropriations bills committee report providing $2.5 million to fund four additional SCI Model Systems. United Spinal continues advocating for appropriations for the Department of Defenses Spinal Cord Injury Research Program (SCIRP). United Spinal advocated for publishing notices of opportunities for funding for the National Model Systems Centers for spinal cord injury with the Administration for Community Living. United Spinal continues to support timely wheelchair repairs legislation that is currently being drafted in the Senate. United Spinal supports and advocates for H. R. 9364, the FAST Repairs for Wheelchairs Act which Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-MA) introduced. The bill would prohibit Medicare Advantage plans from requiring prior authorization for wheelchair repairs. United Spinal advocated for passage of S. Res. 925, a resolution designating September 2026 as "National Spinal Cord Injury Awareness Month" United Spinal staff participated in the Spinal Cord Injury Patient Focused Drug Development meeting supported by the Food and Drug Administration. United Spinal staff participated in the 2026 NINDS Nonprofit Forum on August 14. United Spinal staff attended a congressional briefing about improving the process for drug therapy approval through the Food and Drug Administration. United Spinal staff met with officials from the Administration on Community Living to advocate for a number of issues, including the Spinal Cord Injury Model System program and automated wheelchair securement in modes of transportation. United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organization as members of the Partnership to Improve Patient Care (PIPC), wrote in response to the Senate Finance Committee minority staffs request for information (RFI), Commonsense Policy Options to Lower Drug Prices for Patients. United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Disability and Rehabilitation Research Coalition (DRRC), work to the administrator of the Administration for community living to offer thanks for releasing multiple important Notices of Funding Opportunities (NOFOs) in late June and July for National Institute on Disability, Independent Living, and Rehabilitation Research (NIDILRR) grant competitions, and to request information about the rationale for, and the implications of, removing the remaining Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 NOFOs from www.grants.gov. The letter read in part, With only two months remaining in the fiscal year, the disability and rehabilitation research communitys growing concerns have reached a critical threshold. At this point, we seriously question whether NIDILRR will be able to obligate its full FY 2026 appropriations and maintain the continuity of the nations disability and rehabilitation research enterprise. Members of the Disability and Aging Collaborative (DAC) and United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Long Term Services and Supports (LTSS) Taskforce of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD), wrote to the bipartisan, bicameral leadership of the Congress to urge passage of legislation to extend two critical bipartisan provisions that make community living a reality for people with disabilities and older adults: the Money Follows the Person (MFP) program and spousal impoverishment protections. The letter read in part, Without congressional action, these programs will expire on September 30, 2027. As that funding deadline approaches, states are already making decisions about whether they can continue the extremely successful MFP program. We urge Congress to take action this year to ensure MFP and the spousal impoverishment protections continue. United Spinal provided a letter of support for the renewal of the University of Alabama at Birmingham Spinal Cord Injury Model System (UAB-SCIMS). UAB-SCIMS has been an active partner and participant in United Spinals Maximizing Rehabilitation Outcomes Coalition (MRO). The MRO Coalition is comprised of multiple stakeholders including people with SCI experience, advocates, health care professionals and researchers uniting to address barriers and systemic issues impacting rehabilitation services for people with SCI. UAB-SCIMS participation in our MRO helped construct A Guide to Inpatient Rehabilitation Services for People With Spinal Cord Injury, developed in collaboration with the Model Systems Knowledge Translation Center. Most recently we have been examining the implications of how various lengths of stay in rehabilitation settings can affect rehabilitation outcomes for individuals. United Spinal wrote a letter fully supporting the renewal of the University of Alabama at Birmingham Spinal Cord Injury Model System (UAB-SCIMS). The letter read in part, We also work collaboratively with Spinal Cord Injury Model (SCI) System Centers and the Model Systems Knowledge Translation Center that provide innovative research and support in the field of SCI UAB-SCIMS has been an active partner and participant in United Spinals Maximizing Rehabilitation Outcomes Coalition (MRO).

lobbying_activities.description: United Spinal continues to engage our concerns with the implementation and impact of the community engagement requirements or work requirements, requiring some people to complete at least 80 hours of work, volunteering, school, or training per month to maintain their Medicaid eligibility as required with the enactment of H.R. 1, the 2025 reconciliation law, once called the One Big Beautiful Bill, signed by President Trump on July 4, 2025. United Spinal advocated for passage of H.R. 8540 / S.5321, the HCBS Access Act. The bill would make home and community-based services, HCBS, a mandatory Medicaid benefit, ensuring eligible individuals can choose between receiving care at home or in an institutional setting. United Spinal continues to advocate for Medicare coverage for beneficiaries reimbursement of wheelchair standing systems which allow power wheelchair users to accrue the health benefits of standing thus lowering medical costs. United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Independence Through Enhancement of Medicare and Medicaid (ITEM) Coalition wrote to the bipartisan, bicameral Senate and Senate Finance Committee leadership to urge prompt consideration and pass H.R. 1703, the Choices for Increased Mobility Act. The letter read in part, Having passed the House of Representatives with bipartisan support, H.R. 1703 now presents the Senate with an opportunity to improve Medicare beneficiaries access to clinically appropriate lightweight wheelchair technology. Specifically, the legislation would direct the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish separate Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS) billing codes and payment rates for ultra-lightweight manual wheelchair bases constructed with titanium or carbon fiber, ensuring that Medicare payment policy appropriately recognizes these advanced mobility technologies and improves beneficiary access to them. United Spinal advocated for passage of S. 5428 the Stop the Wait Act. The bill would: Phase out the five-month waiting period for SSDI benefits over the next five years, eliminating it entirely by 2031; and eliminate the 24-month waiting period for Medicare disability benefits for individuals who are uninsured or unable to afford health insurance. Press release listing United Spinal endorsement: https://www.kim.senate.gov/press_release/senator-kim-introduces-bill-to-eliminate-delays-for-americans-with-disabilities-to-receive-social-security-and-medicare-benefits/ Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/5428 United Spinal, along with numerous other organizations and as members of the Independence Through Enhancement of Medicare and Medicaid (ITEM) Coalition wrote the bill sponsors to express our strong support for S. 5475, the Timely Access to Coverage Decisions Act. The letter read in part, This much-needed bipartisan and bicameral legislation includes critical reforms that would create a more predictable and patient-centered Medicare coverage determination process that better supports access to innovation while preserving appropriate clinical and programmatic oversight. We commend you for your leadership in addressing a longstanding challenge within the Medicare program: the absence of clear, accountable, timely, and transparent processes for making coverage decisions that directly affect beneficiary access to care. https://itemcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/item-coalition-letter-of-s.-5475-the-timely-access-to-coverage-decisions-act-final.pdf United Spinal advocated for the legislation supported by NCARTs CRT Awareness Week, September 14th through the 18th. This annual event was created and promoted by the CRT industry and all stakeholders to promote the incredible value that CRT brings to the lives of individuals who rely on this equipment. Included coordinating advocacy to urge the United States Senate to pass the Choices for Increased Mobility Act. United Spinal continues to advocate against implementation of CMS competitive bidding for ostomy and urological supplies. As members of the ITEM Coalition will advocate for individuals to sign a petition to CMS as part of our continued advocacy to stop implementation of competitive bidding for these essential supplies. United Spinal, along with numerous other organizations and as members of the Independence Through Enhancement of Medicare and Medicaid (ITEM) Coalition, wrote to the bipartisan, bicameral leadership of Congress to share new data that should prompt Congress to reconsider implementation of the Round 2028 Remote Item Delivery (RID) Competitive Bidding Program (CBP). The letter read in part, the nationwide survey of Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies (DMEPOS) suppliers conducted in August 2026 provides compelling real-world evidence that the untested RID system could substantially disrupt the supplier infrastructure on which Medicare beneficiaries depend for timely access to ostomy and urological supplies. We respectfully request an opportunity to meet with Congressional leadership to discuss these findings and the significant implications they have for the stability of the DMEPOS supplier network and access to these essential supplies. https://itemcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/item-coalition-letter-to-congress-re-rid-cbp-and-reiterated-access-concerns-final.pdf United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members members of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD) Long Term Services and Supports (LTSS) Task Force, wrote to the bipartisan leadership of the Senate to urge they schedule the Recognizing the Role of Direct Support Professionals Act, a bill that would help to create a standard occupational classification (SOC) for direct support professionals (DSPs), for floor action upon the Senates return from recess in September. On August 5, 2026, the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee passed the bipartisan legislation, S. 3211, introduced by Sen. Hassan (D-NH) and Sen. Collins (R-ME), which ensures that when the Office of Management and Budget revises the standard occupational classification system, it considers the importance of a code for DSPs United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Independence Through Enhancement of Medicare and Medicaid (ITEM), submitted comments in response to the Centers for Medicaid and Medicare Services Calendar Year 2027 Home Health Prospective Payment System Proposed Rule (CMS-1844-P). The comments read in part, The ITEM Coalition strongly supports CMSs long-standing efforts to protect the Medicare program and beneficiaries from fraud, waste, and abuse. Program integrity is essential to protecting beneficiaries and ensuring that Medicare resources remain available to meet the medically. necessary device-based needs of beneficiaries. However, program integrity policies must be carefully designed so that efforts to exclude fraudulent actors do not inadvertently drive legitimate suppliers out of the Medicare program, reduce beneficiary choice, disrupt established supplier relationships, or create barriers to medically necessary assistive devices and technologies. https://itemcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/item-coalition-comments-in-response-to-cy-2027-hh-pps-proposed-rule-final.pdf United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Long Term Services and Supports, Health, and Rights Task Forces of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD) or the Disability and Aging Collaborative (DAC) wrote to the administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services to comment on the Interim Final Rule with comment period Medicaid Program; Community Engagement Requirement for Certain Individuals (Interim Final Rule or IFC) implementing the Medicaid community engagement requirements under section 1902(xx) of the Social Security Act, as added by section 71119 of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) (Pub. L. 119-21), RIN 0938-AV98; CMS-2454-IFC. The comments read in part, We write to express our deep concern regarding the impact of the Interim Final Rule with Comment Period (IFC) on individuals with disabilities, older adults, and family caregivers and our strong opposition to several policies in the IFC, including expanded restriction and administrative barriers that will put coverage at risk for our constituencies. These burdens disproportionately impact older adults and people with disabilities who have a harder time finding work and maintaining employment due to functional limitations, changing work or caregiving responsibilities, and fluctuating health. For example, the vast majority of older adults ages 50-64 enrolled in Medicaid expansion who are retired or not working (86%) report having a health condition that prevents them from working. https://downloads.regulations.gov/CMS-2026-2047-42435/attachment_1.pdf United Spinal provided a letter to the Medicare Contractor for Pricing, Data Analysis and Coding (PDAC) expressing serious concerns about a code verification decision issued on May 27, 2026, concluding that ONWARD Medicals ARC-EX System for at-home use is not billable to the Durable Medical Equipment Medicare Administrative Contractors (DME MACs) because it was determined not to qualify as durable medical equipment (DME) and was characterized primarily as a rehabilitative exercise tool. The letter read in part, As the field of neurological treatment for SCI continues to evolve, Medicare coverage and coding policies must keep pace with innovation. Spinal cord stimulation devices such as the ARC-EX System represent a significant advancement in SCI care, offering meaningful opportunities to improve functional outcomes and independence for individuals living with chronic incomplete SCI. Medicare decisions that narrowly categorize these technologies as mere exercise tools fail to reflect the clinical realities of SCI, the impact these interventions can have on daily function and independence, and the chilling effect created for future technologies to assist the SCI population. United Spinal, along with numerous other organizations, 490 total, as members of the Disability and Aging Collaborative (DAC), the Health and Long-Term Services and Supports (LTSS) Task forces of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD), and allied organizations wrote to the bipartisan, bicameral leadership and members of Congress to urge they exclude any funding cuts or harmful changes to Medicaid from any budget reconciliation or other legislation. The letter read in part, Medicaid is our communities lifeline, and that lifeline just suffered the largest cut in funding since its inception. We cannot afford any further cuts, and we urge Congress to prioritize reinvesting in Medicaid. https://c-c-d.org/fichiers/DAC_CCD-LTSS-Health-July-26-Sign-On-Letter-Opposing-Medicaid-Cuts-in-Reconciliation.pdf United Spinal wrote to the PDAC-Medicare Contractor Palmetto GBA to express serious concerns regarding the Medicare Contractor for Pricing, Data Analysis and Coding (PDAC) code verification decision issued on May 27, 2026, concluding that ONWARD Medicals ARC-EX System for at-home use is not billable to the Durable Medical Equipment Medicare Administrative Contractors (DME MACs) because it was determined not to qualify as durable medical equipment (DME) and was characterized primarily as a rehabilitative exercise tool. United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Independence Through Enhancement of Medicare and Medicaid (ITEM) Coalition wrote to the sponsors of H.R. 8500, the Timely Access to Coverage Decisions Act to express our strong support for that legislation. The letter in part read, This much-needed bipartisan legislation includes critical reforms that would create a more predictable and patient-centered Medicare coverage determination process that better supports access to innovation while preserving appropriate clinical and programmatic oversight. We commend you for your leadership in addressing a longstanding challenge within the Medicare program: the absence of clear, accountable, timely, and transparent processes for making coverage decisions that directly affect beneficiary access to care. United Spinal continues to advocate for forthcoming legislation that will exclude ostomy and urological supplies from Medicares durable medical equipment, prosthetics, orthotics, and supplies (DMEPOS) competitive bidding program for a period of five years while requiring the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to undertake a more comprehensive and clinically informed review of the impact that competitive bidding policies could have on beneficiary access, product choice, and patient outcomes. And other related provisions. United Spinal continues to urge Members of Congress to protect and strengthen home and community-based services (HCBS), which already operates within a fragile system challenged by workforce shortages, long waiting lists, and inadequate funding. Millions of older adults and people with disabilities rely on HCBS to live independently in their homes and communities, and demand for these services will continue to grow as the population ages. Further cuts or restrictions would worsen existing barriers, increase the risk of institutionalization, and leave many without the support they need. Investing in and preserving HCBS is essential to ensure current and future generations can access quality care at home.

lobbying_activities.description: United Spinal discussed provisions of H.R.8128, the Same-Day Paratransit Innovation Act, with congressional staff. United Spinal continues to advocate for accessibility provisions to be included in H. R. 8870, the BUILD America 250 Act. United Spinal, as a co-lead of our SecureRide Coalition, continues to advocate for deployable anchor rest study provision in Section 15 of H. R. 7389, the Motor Vehicle Safety Modernization Act https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/7389/text United Spinal staff helped coordinate our SecureRide Coalitions participation in the Department of Transportations first ever Roadway Safety Innovation Expo United Spinal staff met with various officials throughout the Department of Transportation as part of our SecureRides advocacy for automated wheelchair securement in vehicles. And we continue to engage with two NHTSA SBIR grant awardees on automated wheelchair securement as part of our SecureRide advocacy. United Spinals SecureRide Coalition provided a letter of support to the University of Michigan Transportation Research Institute about wheelchair securement for a grant submission to the Federal Transit Administration, FTA-2026-004-TRI https://www.transit.dot.gov/notices-funding/fy-2026-notice-funding-opportunity-bus-safety-accessibility-and-innovation-research United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations, and as members of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD) Transportation Task Force submitted comments in response to the Department of Transportations Request for Information on Family Friendly Transit. The comments read in part, We appreciate the Federal Transit Administrations (FTA) consideration of ways to improve measurement of whether transit services serve all people, including families. Because people with disabilities have unique travel needs at every age, we urge you to prioritize accessibility and availability of transit services when considering how transit options serve families. In these comments, we oﬀer our perspective on ways to include people with disabilities in these eﬀorts. We identify questions that can inform existing and new data collections to improve transportation access for people with disabilities and their families within the five identified areas. https://c-c-d.org/fichiers/CCD-Transportation-Comments-on-Family-Friendly-Transit-RFI-July2026.pdf United Spinal submitted comments in response to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administrations Guidance: Safe Development and Deployment of Automated Driving Systems, Docket: NHTSA-2026-1520. The letter read in part, We also appreciate the National Highway Traffic Safety Administrations (NHTSA) continued efforts to advance a national regulatory effort in which the next generation of transportation, autonomous vehicles, can be deployed to operate on Americas roadways safely. As you have said, access to transportation is access to freedom. Autonomous vehicles (AV) hold the promise of the access for wheelchair users and others in our community that you envision. https://downloads.regulations.gov/NHTSA-2026-1520-0014/attachment_1.pdf United Spinal provided a letter of support for the University of Michigan Transportation Research Institutes (UMTRI) proposal titled, Secure Transit for All: Advancing Bus Passenger Safety and Innovating Wheelchair Securement, in response to the Federal Transit Authoritys (FTA) request for proposals to conduct research to improve the safety and accessibility on buses. United Spinal continues to advocate for H.R. 4116, the Disability Access to Transportation Act (DATA) Paratransit one stop and data collection pilot program. The bill would establish an extra stop per trip program for passengers using paratransit serves and enhance data collection for paratransit programs to increase accessible transportation for individuals with disabilities. United Spinal advocated for its SecureRide Coalition wheelchair securement standard efforts with Administration for Community Living officials. United Spinal advocated for its SecureRide Coalition wheelchair securement standard efforts with Access Board officials. United Spinal advocated for its SecureRide Coalition wheelchair securement standard efforts with National Council on Disability officials. United Spinal advocated for the bipartisan All Stations Accessibility Program (ASAP) Reauthorization Act (S. 5086) is a bipartisan bill introduced in July 2026 by U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and Dave McCormick (R-PA) to renew and continue funding the federal All Stations Accessibility Program. And the House companion bill, Introduced by Rep. Jesus Chuy Garcia (D-IL) and Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA. This bill would continue funding a federal program that makes older rail stations accessible four people with disabilities. United Spinal staff extended an invitation to a Senator to provide a welcome message for an SAE accessibility challenge for college engineering students designing for people with disabilities utilizing autonomous vehicles.

lobbying_activities.description: United Spinal has expressed similar concerns about H.R. 8884, the Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act, that were shared with the bipartisan leadership of the House by the co-chairs of the Social Security Task Force (SSTF) of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD). The co-chairs wrote: a crucial principle for the design of all demonstration projects is the protection of a claimants total benefits. This is critical. Disabled beneficiaries who are agreeing to be part of an experiment need to be held harmless. They should not be provided less than what non-participants are receiving. Moreover, offering this protection is critical to the recruitment of participants to ensure the success of the demonstration. We are concerned that, as written, H.R. 8884 does not provide this commonsense guardrail. United Spinal supported a letter the cochairs of the Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD) Social Security Task Force wrote to the Senate sponsors of the Work Without Worry Act. The letter thanked the senators for introducing this crucial legislation and read in part, Unfortunately, the disabled adult child (DAC) programs strict rules related to work are extremely challenging for people with disabilities and their families to navigate. Under current rules, if a young person with disability has countable earnings of even a dollar over the substantial gainful activity (SGA) level ($1690 for non-blind individuals in 2026) before receiving DAC benefits, they lose their eligibility for DAC benefits forever.

lobbying_activities.description: United Spinal continues to advocate against an Office of Management and Budget policy change that would harm federal grant programs. On May 29th, OMB proposed a rule for federal grants and other forms of federal assistance that would dramatically increase political control over scientific research funding across the U.S. government. United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as members of the Disability and Rehabilitation Research Coalition (DRRC) we appreciate the opportunity to submit these comments in strong opposition to the Office of Management and Budgets (OMB) proposed rule revising the Uniform Guidance for Federal Financial Assistance, codified at 2 C.F.R. Part 200 (hereafter referred to as the Proposed Rule), (OMB-2026-0034). The comments read in part, While presented as a grants management reform initiative, this proposed rule would fundamentally alter longstanding principles that have governed federal research funding for decades. Collectively, the proposed changes included in this proposed rule threaten to undermine the stability, independence, and effectiveness of the federal research enterprise at a time when continued investment in evidence-based innovation is essential to improving health outcomes, advancing rehabilitation science, and addressing the needs of millions of individuals with disabilities and other chronic condition. United Spinal, along with numerous other disability organizations as member Consortium for Constituents with Disabilities (CCD) Developmental Disabilities, Autism and Family Support, Health, Housing, Long Term Services and Supports, and Rights Task Forces, and allies, write to express our strong opposition to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB)s Proposed Regulation regarding federal financial assistance, [2 CFR 200.205, 200.300, 200.340-200.343, 200.421, 200.450] 91 Fed.Reg. 32198 (May 29, 2026); RIN OMB-2026-0034-0001. The comments read in part: If finalized, the rule would alter the requirements for recipients of federal financial assistance from more than 40 federal agencies. United Spinal, along with the American Association of People with Disabilities (AAPD) and 38 other organizations submitted comments in response to the Office of Management and Budgets (OMB) proposed revisions to the Uniform Guidance governing federal financial assistance, RIN 0348-AB88. The comments read in part, Federal financial assistance is central to the nations disability infrastructure, supporting direct services, independent living, civil rights enforcement, systems advocacy, research, technical assistance, and community-based services. We support effective stewardship of federal funds. However, we are concerned that the proposed rule: 1. Expands agency discretion in ways that may blur statutory limits on federal grant programs; 2. Uses broadly defined concepts such as authorized public purpose without sufficient clarity; 3. Creates uncertainty regarding permissible activities under federal awards; 4. Risks chilling lawful and Congressionally authorized activities, including advocacy, systems analysis, and research; 5. Expands enforcement authority without corresponding procedural safeguards; and 6. May adversely affect nonprofit and disability-led organizations that rely on stable and predictable federal funding.

lobbying_activities.description: H.R. 3514/S. 1816: Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act of 2025 - requires Medicare Advantage plans to implement electronic prior authorization, increase transparency, protect enrollees, and adhere to new response timeframes to improve timely access to care. H.R. 2433: Reducing Medically Unnecessary Delays in Care Act - mandates that prior authorization decisions under Medicare be made by qualified physicians, based on medical necessity and evidence-based standards, with transparency and input from practicing physicians. H.R. 9693, Patients First Act of 2026 would finally make structural changes needed to prevent cuts and create a payment system that helps ensure physicians can keep their doors open and provide seniors with quality, value-based healthcare. S. 1640/H.R. 879: Medicare Patient Access and Practice Stabilization Act of 2025 - This bill increases certain payment adjustments under the Medicare physician fee schedule for services furnished between April 1, 2025, and January 1, 2026. H.R. 8163/S. 5180: Provider Reimbursement Stability Act, to amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure stability for provider payments under the Medicare program. H.R. 8622: Medicare Physician Data-driven Performance Payment System Act to amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to transform the Merit-based Incentive Payment System into the Data-driven Performance Payment System under the Medicare physician fee schedule H.R. 6160: Strengthening Medicare for Patients and Providers Act to modify certain adjustments to payment amounts under the Medicare physician fee schedule S. 1460/H.R. 786: Preserving Patient Access to Accountable Care Act - extends Medicare incentive payments for alternative payment models to 2027, with a new rate of 3.53 percent, to promote continued participation and improve healthcare efficiency. H.R. 2120/S. 1031: ROCR Value Based Program Act - establishes a new payment program for radiation oncology services, focusing on stable payments, quality care, and patient access, while exempting it from budget neutrality adjustments. H.R. 4559: Prompt and Fair Pay Act - to establish payment parity between Medicare Advantage and fee-for-service Medicare, and to establish prompt payment requirements under Medicare Advantage. H.R. 2484: Seniors' Access to Critical Medications Act of 2025 - establishes an exception to the physician self-referral prohibition for certain outpatient drugs under Medicare, mandates a study on drug dispensing practices, and reduces the Medicare improvement fund by $18 million. H.R. 4299: Protecting Patient Access to Cancer and Complex Therapies Act - provide for a rebate by manufacturers for selected drugs and biological products subject to maximum fair price negotiation. H.R. 4206/S. 1261: CONNECT for Health Act - expands access to telehealth services under Medicare H.R. 5081/S. 2709: Telehealth Modernization Act - to extend certain telehealth flexibilities under the Medicare program. H.R. 4752/S. 2760: Reducing Hereditary Cancer Act - to provide hereditary cancer genetic testing for individuals with a history of a hereditary cancer gene mutation. H.R. 8500: Timely Access to Coverage Decisions Act of 2026: To amend title XVIII of the Social Security Act to ensure timely review of local coverage determination requests under the Medicare program. H.R. 4331, Access to Claims Data Act: To require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a process to expand access to claims data under certain Federal health plans in order to facilitate research and quality improvement.

H.R. 6423/S. 864: HELP Copays Act - requires health insurers to count third-party financial assistance toward patients' cost-sharing obligations, including deductibles and copays, for prescription drugs, with changes effective for plan years beginning January 1, 2026. S. 526: PBM Transparency Act - prevents unfair and deceptive acts or practices and the dissemination of false information related to pharmacy benefit management services for prescription drugs H.R. 4191/S. 1784: MAPS Act - requires federal agencies to regularly update a list of essential medicines, assess and report on supply chain risks, map pharmaceutical supply chains, and enhance coordination and cybersecurity to protect public health and national security. H.R. 3955/S.2062: RAPID Reserve Act - establishes a $500 million program to create and maintain domestic reserves of critical drugs and their ingredients, prioritizing domestic manufacturing and supply chain resilience to prevent shortages during public health emergencies. H.R. 8339: Drug Origin Transparency Act to amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to enhance drug manufacturing amount information reporting H.R. 5526/S. 1954: Biosimilar Red Tape Elimination Act - streamlines the approval process for biosimilar biological products by automatically deeming them interchangeable with reference products, subject to certain exclusivity protections, and requires updated regulatory guidance to reflect these changes. H.R. 4101: Cancer Drug Parity Act of 2025 - requires group health plans to provide cost-sharing for oral anticancer drugs that is at least as favorable as for provider-administered anticancer medications, with protections against increased patient costs and a mandated GAO study on the law's impact. H.R. 3521/S. 4440: Clinical Trials Modernization Act - Increase clinical trial participation among underrepresented populations by providing grants, permitting certain participant reimbursements, and offering tax exclusions, while ensuring compliance with existing legal protections. S. 705: Innovation in Pediatric Drugs Act of 2025 - amends existing laws to enhance pediatric cancer research, mandates compliance measures, allocates funding for pediatric studies, and sets guidelines for orphan drugs, with specific timelines for implementation and evaluation. H.R. 5509/S. 2903: Safe Step Act - to require a group health plan or health insurance coverage offered in connection with such a plan to provide an exceptions process for any medication step therapy protocol, and for other purposes. H.R. 4425/S. 2287: Palliative Care and Hospice Education and Training Act - expands federal support for workforce development, education, public awareness, and research in palliative and hospice care, with targeted funding and statutory changes to improve care for patients with serious or life-threatening illnesses. H.R. 8839/S. 5052: Lainie Jones Comprehensive Cancer Survivorship Act of 2026 to address the health of cancer survivors.

lobbying_activities.description: $3M CDS request - HUD EDI (THUD): The Central Washington Applied Technology and Entrepreneurship Center will adaptively reuse the historic 18,000 sq. ft. Old Heat building (509 E. University Way, Ellensburg) as central Washingtons first dedicated technology commercialization hub. The facility will house advanced manufacturing prototyping, applied research, startup incubation, and workforce development programs - anchored by CWUs applied engineering, computer science, and physics programs and designed to attract aerospace supply chain, agricultural technology, clean technology, and advanced materials tenants. $2.09M CDS request - NIST STRS / CJS: Integrated Drone Program is a two-site initiative: a centralized commercial-grade drone fleet at CWU's Ellensburg campus serving nine academic programs and regional industry workers, paired with Phase 1 of an outdoor BVLOS-capable test range at Deer Park Airport (Spokane County) - the first dedicated public-access outdoor UAS range in eastern Washington. Eastern and central Washington - a largely rural region spanning nearly 45,000 square miles - has no centralized public UAS training infrastructure and no dedicated outdoor BVLOS test range within 100 miles of any comparable institution. The FAA projects the Part 107 certified commercial pilot workforce will grow from 427,598 (2024) to 522,325+ by 2029, driven by surging employer demand in construction, energy, agriculture, public safety, and emergency response. Regional employers including Washington DNR, Avista Utilities, WSDOT, and eastern Washington agricultural operations face a workforce gap they cannot fill from the current pipeline.
